question:
Find the volume (in cm³) of the largest right circular cone that can be cut out from a cube with an edge of 8 cm.

Use pi = (22)/(7)
solution:
**Given:**

Edge of the cube = 8 cm

**Formula Used:**

For the largest right circular cone cut from a cube:

Diameter of the base of the cone = Edge of the cube

Height of the cone = Edge of the cube

Volume of a cone = 1/3 × π × r² × h

Where, r = radius, h = height

**Calculations:**

Diameter of the cone = 8 cm

⇒ Radius (r) = 8/2 = 4 cm

Height (h) = 8 cm

Volume of the cone = 1/3 × (22/7) × 4² × 8

⇒ Volume of the cone = 1/3 × (22/7) × 16 × 8

⇒ Volume of the cone = (22 × 16 × 8) / (3 × 7)

⇒ Volume of the cone = 2816 / 21

⇒ Volume of the cone ≈ 134(2)/(21) cm³

**∴ The volume of the largest right circular cone that can be cut out from a cube with an edge of 8 cm is **134(2)/(21)** **cm3
